Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a widened superior mediastinum with bilateral paratracheal fullness that is more prominent on the right side, causing mass effect and displacement of the trachea to the left. This appearance is characteristic of significant lymphadenopathy (such as in lymphoma), which fits the clinical presentation of an 11-year-old with retrosternal pain, rather than lung collapse or pleural effusion.
